tldr: Each webhook now has payloadGeneration: DEFERRED, the default, or IMMEDIATE. An IMMEDIATE webhook gets its payload built when the event fires, with the state of that moment.
goal: Let an app that applies each event in sequence get the state at trigger time, while other webhooks keep deferred payloads.

story.heading: Webhook gets a payload_generation field
story.body: The new column is deferred by default. Existing webhooks keep deferred payloads, so they behave as before.

story.heading: Async triggers split the webhooks of an event
story.body: DEFERRED webhooks go to the background task. IMMEDIATE ones get their payload at once, and only they slow the request down.

story.heading: Apps set it; webhookTrigger respects it
story.body: The manifest, webhookCreate and webhookUpdate take DEFERRED or IMMEDIATE. A manual trigger defers only for a DEFERRED webhook.

story.heading: ADR 0011 records the trade-off
story.body: Deferred payloads carry the state when the task runs, not when the event happened. The opt-out is for consumers that need each step.

components.summary: New WebhookPayloadGenerationEnum; webhookCreate and webhookUpdate set it, and webhookTrigger reads it.
The app manifest takes payloadGeneration per webhook and stores deferred when it is missing.
Webhook stores payload_generation. Async triggers build IMMEDIATE payloads at once and defer the rest.

decisions.title: Deferred stays the default; IMMEDIATE is a per-webhook opt-out
decisions.why: Deferral keeps heavy mutations fast. An integration that applies each ORDER_METADATA_UPDATED in sequence breaks when all deliveries carry the final state.
decisions.alternative: Store a snapshot of every payload in the request.

decisions.title: The setting is read once, when the delivery is created
decisions.why: Deliveries and queued tasks finish the way they started. A later change of the setting affects only new deliveries.
decisions.alternative: Read the setting again when the task runs.

decisions.title: An IMMEDIATE payload reads from the writer
decisions.why: A task can fire the event right after its own write. The replica can lag, so dataloaders read the writer for this path.
decisions.alternative: Read the replica, as the deferred task does.

decisions.title: Group the webhooks, not the event
decisions.why: An event reaches many apps. Each app chooses for its own webhook, and only that webhook pays the cost.
decisions.alternative: A setting per event type for all apps.
